An English crib of the Latin text, semi-literal, made for this database in 2026 with Claude, a large language model (LLM) made by Anthropic. It keeps close to the wording of the original and uses the established English of Anglo-Latin legal, liturgical and canon-law formulae. It is an aid to reading the original, not a published translation. Square brackets mark Liebermann’s additions to the text or, now and then, words supplied for the sense; “[?]” marks a doubtful reading

div.head: ECf 36.1
div.ab: Et detur ei terminus unius mensis, ut habeat parentes interfecti ex utraque parte generis sui, scilicet ex parte patris XII et ex parte matris VI.
div.note: Liebermann’s text transcribed from Gesetze I p. 666 (November 2026): read from the page images and checked against the scan’s own text layer, differences settled against the page.

div.ab: And let a term of one month be given him, that he may have kinsmen of the slain man from both sides of his kin, namely on the father's side twelve and on the mother's side six.
